nodes.label: 4T8 ClassicPonder with 4 pluggable line ports, 12 clients (4CP4T8)
nodes.detail: The 4CP4T8 is a 4.8 Tbps quad-line add/drop muxponder for the PSS-hc platform with 12x pluggable QSFP-DD client ports and 4x pluggable line ports compatible with high-performance PSE6s modules BMDCO12E (C-band) and BMDCO12LE (L-band). The single slot 4CP4T8 leverages high-performance Nokia PSE-6s coherent optical engines to provide up to 4.8 Tb/s coherent line capacity. The PSE-6s supports up to 140 Gbaud and 1.2 Tb/s per wavelength and leverages a comprehensive coherent toolkit including 3rd-generation probabilistic constellation shaping, continuously tuneable baud rate, C-band and L-band support, overhead efficient Ethernet framing mode, high chromatic dispersion tolerance, and encryption. Each 4CP4T8 supports up to four PSE-6s pluggables, enabling pay-as-you-grow scaling and mixing of C-band and L-band pluggables on the same card. The 4CP4T8 supports eight QSFP56-DD clients (400GbE/OTUC4, 4x100GbE/ OTU4) and four QSFP56-DD/QSFP800 clients (800GbE, 400GbE/OTUC4, 4x100GbE/OTU4). Leveraging 2x100G LR4 QSFP-DDs, the 4CP4T8 can support a configuration with 2x1.2 Tb/s coherent interfaces with up to 20x100G LR4 clients. The 4CP4T8 also support client bandwidth sharing into dual carrier configurations (for example, 5x400GbE over 2x1 Tb/s). The 4CP4T8 card is supported in the 1830 PSS-4hc and PSS-10hc shelves.

nodes.label: 1830 PSS-4II equipment controller, compact (4EC3C)
nodes.detail: 4EC3C is the compact controller variant of 4EC3, and further optimizes performance/cost ratio for typical access applications. Compared with 4EC3, 4EC3C has less storage (40GB vs. 128GB) and less RAM (8GB vs 16GB) and lower power consumption. 4EC3C continues to support –5°C to +65°C operational temperature in 1830 PSS-4II shelves. The migration from 4EC3 to 4EC3C, and mixing of 4EC3 and 4EC3C in a NE are supported.

nodes.label: 1830 PSS-4II 600W AC power card (PMAC600)
nodes.detail: PMAC600 has 600W power output at the backplane at 110V/220V AC input. PMAC600 provides higher power capacity than PMAC500 by 100W, therefore it can support more high-power configurations in an 1830 PSS-4II shelf. PMAC600 continues to support –5°C to +65°C operational ambient temperature, 1+1 AC power card protection, and no AC/DC mixing in one 1830 PSS-4II shelf. The 1830 PSS-4II system supports mixing of PMAC500 and PMAC600 in one shelf in normal operation status, this helps migration from PMAC500 to PMAC600 in multiple steps. Note: When PMAC500 and PMAC600 are both installed in a single shelf, the total shelf power capacity is limited by the PMAC500 (500W at the backplane).

nodes.label: OTDR filter card, C+L band (OTDRFCL)
nodes.detail: The OTDRFCL filter card is introduced to provide OTDR function per fiber direction in C+L OLP configurations. The OTDRFCL is a one-slot width and half-height card with two OTDR filters with three LC ports each. The OTDRFCL connects to the OPSCL card to support OTDR function through OTDRWB. Supported shelves are 1830 PSS-8, PSS-16II/AC, PSS-32, PSI-4L, and PSI-8L.

nodes.label: Key software features on 16P200
nodes.detail: In 16P200 ODU SNCP configurations, the traffic disruption time can be measured starting from detection of line-side Signal Failure (SF) or Signal Degrade (SD) to the completion of ODU SNCP switching. The measured traffic disruption time measured by 16P200 maps primarily to the interval starting from “SF or SD trigger” (the start of T2) to “Protection switching operations completed” (the end of T4) which are defined in ITU-T G.808.1. Note the traffic disruption time reported by 16P200 is not the total traffic restoration time starting from “Network impairment” (the start of T1) to “Protected traffic fully restored” (the end of T5) as defined in ITU-T G.808.1 as T1 and T5 are out of detection scope of 16P200. 16P200 ODU SNCP traffic disruption time measurement function can be disabled (default) and enabled through provisioning parameter tdtm-enabled at an egress ODUNIM or ODUPTF facility. The measured time can be retrieved with the parameter tdtm-result, and up to 100 times of measurement (provisionable, 10 as default) can be stored and retrieved. (Q28LR4E, PN: 3AL82219AA).

nodes.label: Secure boot sequence lockdown
nodes.detail: A new system-wide setting lets you block unauthenticated access to the bootloader over the serial console. When enabled, the system prevents users connected via serial console to interrupt the boot process and access the bootloader. The option can be toggled (enable/disable) via any 1830 PSS management interface, allowing you to keep the lock active in production while still permitting temporary debug or integration access when needed.

nodes.label: USB port lockdown for equipment controllers and shelf panels
nodes.detail: A single system-wide setting enables or disables the USB ports on equipment controller packs and shelf user panels. When disabled, auto-mount and USB-based scratch-install functions are blocked, preventing USB access to the network element. The feature is available across all supported 1830 PSS management interfaces, including YANG-based APIs, and can be controlled through CLI, NETCONF, or external orchestration systems.

nodes.label: Electrical shelf power-consumption telemetry
nodes.detail: The input current/voltage, and (for PF units) output current, voltage, and power are retrievable on-demand and streamed on the NETCONF and gRPC management interface using the OpenConfig Platform YANG module. The minimal reporting interval for this data is 60 sec. Any subscription requesting a lower reporting interval for this data than the minimum value will be treated as reporting interval of 60 sec.

nodes.label: LED-based hardware Identification
nodes.detail: This feature enables on-site technicians to quickly locate a specific shelf, card, or optical module by triggering all LEDs on the selected hardware to blink in a controlled pattern. The blinking helps visually distinguish the target component from surrounding equipment.

nodes.label: SSH host certificate authentication
nodes.detail: The 1830 PSS now supports OpenSSH host certificate authentication across all SSH-based management interfaces. This allows operators to securely verify the identity of the network element using certificate-based host keys (RSA, ECDSA, ED25519). The system provides the required key pairs, supports multiple certificates, and includes a built-in PKI for certificate provisioning and rotation. Configuration is available via Classic CLI,NETCONF, gRPC, and OpenConfig YANG.

nodes.label: 1830 PSS-4hc/10hc reset button
nodes.detail: The system provides three reset functions using a single hardware reset button, each activated by a simple press pattern and indicated by EPS LED signals. A long press triggers a full controller restart on any controller, while two shorter press-and-release sequences on the main active controller allow customers to clear the configuration database or clear both configuration and IP settings. These reset options offer a quick and reliable way to recover the system without requiring software access. This ensures fast troubleshooting and restores normal operation with minimal effort.

nodes.label: SyncE and PTP insertion/extraction on S13X400E/H
nodes.detail: This feature provides in-band synchronization (SyncE and PTP insertion/extraction) over the 10GbE/100GbE client interfaces of the S13X400E/S13X400H. Synchronization data carried on the 10GbE/100GbE client signals can be extracted by the card from the customer's data streams received on the client ports and processed by the F-CRU cards of the 1830 PSS-8/16II. Working together with PTPIOC/SYNCTL and the F-CRU cards, the network side separates the synchronization signals from the customer's traffic and transports them through the bi-directional OTC channel. The remaining 10GbE traffic after extracting synchronization data is mapped to an ODU2 payload through GFP-F. The remaining 100GE traffic after extracting synchronization data is mapped to an ODU4 payload through GFP-F and ODUflex. On the client side, the synchronization data is re-inserted into the egress streams, enabling in-band transmission of synchronization information.

nodes.label: SYNCTL card support in 1830 PSI-4L shelves
nodes.detail: The SYNCTL card is supported on the 1830 PSI-4L shelves with four working modes: local clock mode, local clock extension mode, LambdaConversion mode, and relay mode. Security The following are the new Security-related features in Release 26.6:

nodes.label: OSPFv3 Security Authentication Trailer
nodes.detail: OSPFv3 Security Authentication Trailer enhances routing security by authenticating OSPFv3 routing updates. It supports modern, stronger cryptographic authentication algorithms from the SHA-2 family (such as SHA-256 and SHA-512), in addition to the available MD5-based protection. Authentication can be enabled or disabled per OSPF interface, giving operators flexibility to meet their security and operational requirements.

nodes.label: Transit BGP routes
nodes.detail: This feature allows the external DCN to reach a BGP network connected through the 1830 DCN. With this feature, the BGP and OSPF routing protocols policies are implemented to forward traffic from an external Autonomous System (AS) across the 1830 DCN to another external AS. Thus, the 1830 DCN works as a transit network, exchanging routing information at the GNEs to allow traffic to be forwarded through the 1830 DCN. The identification of transit routes within 1830 DCN is based on OSPF tagging. The outgoing BGP routes distributed by GNE to another external AS can be tagged with BGP community tags. BGP IPv4 routes were previously supported; BGP IPv6 routes are supported in this release.

nodes.label: CMPv2 support on NE
nodes.detail: The 1830 PSS NEs support Certificate Management Protocol (CMP) v2 defined by RFC 4210 toward a Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) CMP server to acquire a Certificate Authority (CA)-signed end-entity (EE) certificate. Only a single signed EE certificate is supported on the NE. New CLI and WebUI commands are available to set CMPv2 server-related configuration parameters (for example: port, IP address, pre-shared key) and send CMP certificate requests. The NE supports the following CMP certificate requests: initialization request, key update request, and polling for status of message requests.

nodes.label: Secure Server-Side File Transfer
nodes.detail: The 1830 PSS Network Element (NE) can act as a secure file-transfer server, supporting both Secure Copy Protocol (SCP) and Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP). This feature can be used to transfer many different types of files (for example, software image files or database files). Therefore, a separate operation is required to either create a file on the NE to transfer out of the NE or to use a file that has been transferred into the NE.

nodes.label: Secure software validation for 1830 PSS-4hc/10hc shelves
nodes.detail: Software images must be digitally signed. The system verifies the integrity and authenticity of software before installation, ensuring that only trusted software is executed on 1830 PSS-4hc and PSS-10hc platforms. Packet The following packet-related features are available in Release 26.6:

nodes.label: IEEE 802.1X port authentication
nodes.detail: The IEEE 802.1X port-based Network Access Control (PNAC) protocol is supported on the 18CE300, 12CE121, 12CE120, 1CE100Q packet cards and all the associated functionality (EAP authentication, user validation, etc). The goal is to authenticate end devices connected to client ports and protect against unauthorized access or denial-of-service attacks within active services. With this enhancement, L2 UNIs support standards-based security as defined by IEEE 802.1X and RFC 3748 (EAP), strengthening service security and operational reliability.

nodes.label: Key software features on 18CE300
nodes.detail: The QSFP28 I-temp (case temperature –40°C to +85°C) 100GbE LR4 pluggable (Q28LR4E, PN: 3AL82219AA), is supported on the following cards/ports and shelves for 100GbE applications: * Ports C13 and C17 on 16P200 cards in 1830 PSS-4II/8 shelves in system ambient temperature range −5°C to +65°C, if not limited by other cards or pluggables in the shelves. * Ports 17 and 18 on 18CE300 cards in 1830 PSS-4II shelves in system ambient temperature range −5°C to +65°C and PSS-8 shelves in system temperature range −40°C to +65°C, if not limited by other cards or pluggables in the shelves. The 100G ZR DWDM Coherent DCO QSFP28 optical module (QDCO1, PN 3AL82265AB) is supported on the 18CE300 card and can be configured to operate in an extended reach mode supporting distances up to 300 km. This is achieved through enhanced chromatic dispersion compensation of up to 6 ns/nm. The pluggable provides full C-band tunability with 50 GHz and 100 GHz channel spacing granularity and guarantees a transmit output power above –8 dBm. Extended reach (300 km) is enabled through a CMIS register configuration command. Modifying this parameter introduces a brief traffic interruption and is therefore recommended during initial installation. When extended reach mode is enabled, module power consumption increases by approximately 0.2 W, up to a maximum of 6.2 W. Maintaining compatibility with grey, WDM, fixed OADM, flexgrid, and route-and-select applications, this enhancement enables standards-based 100G coherent transport over longer distances on the 18CE300 without requiring an uplink card. In the 1830 PSS-32 shelf, the 18CE300 card derives a frequency reference from the SYNCTL synchronization processing card through a 1 GbE connection between a dedicated interworking port on the 18CE300 faceplate (port 12) and an Ethernet port on the SYNCTL card. The 18CE300 card then distributes the frequency reference and the associated ESMC messages to its client Ethernet ports. This functionality enables SyncE distribution to downstream NEs and provides a common frequency reference to the TDM Network Transformation Smart SFP pluggable modules (TPoP, CSoP, TSoP) installed on client ports. ## New features — GMPLS Control Plane 1.3 New features - GMPLS CP
